title: Interactive plan anchoring notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick brain dump to anchor an "interactive" product plan that blends session credits + per-token top-ups. Want something simple for UX but defensible economically for hosted tiers.

High-level idea:
- Sell an "Interactive" starter with X session credits/month + optional token top-ups. Each session credit covers a conversation up to a soft token budget (e.g., 2k tokens). If exceeded, user consumes per-token credits.
- Session credit = billing primitive for interactive UX. Easier UX than pure tokens for chat apps.
- Support roll-ups: add-on token bundles, burst credits for spikes, and metered overage.

Core assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Infra cost (approx): 0.0025 USD per 1k tokens (hosted optimized, quantized weights, cache/batching benefits). Range: 0.0015 - 0.004 depending on model/seq and batching.
- Realized reduction from caching/batching for chat workloads: 15-30% token cost savings typical (assume 20% baseline).
- Average interactive session length (target app): 700 total tokens (prompt+response), median 450, tail 3k+.
- Active sessions per MAU: 6 sessions/mo (power user 25+).
- Target gross margin: 70-80% for hosted SKU (we want room to fund SRE/observability/support).

Simple math examples (anchor numbers):
- Raw cost per average session (700 tokens): 700 / 1000 * 0.0025 = $0.00175; with 20% caching -> $0.0014 per session to infra.
- If we price session credit to customers at $0.02 per session-credit -> gross margin = (0.02 - 0.0014)/0.02 ≈ 93% (very healthy, may be too high).
- Alternative: price session at $0.005 -> margin ≈ 72% (more realistic for starter).

Bundling options to test (UX-first):
- Starter Interactive: 300 session credits/mo + 10k token bundle = $49/mo. (ints: 300*avg session 0.7k -> covers 210k tokens equivalent)
- Growth Interactive: 2k session credits/mo + 80k tokens = $299/mo
- Pay-as-you-go top-up: $0.005 / session-credit (auto top-up), $0.02 / 1k tokens for token top-ups (retail)
- Burst credit add-on (90-day expiry): pack of 2k credits at 20% premium vs monthly unit price (helps cover unused capacity).

Hybrid accounting: convert tokens <-> sessions for reporting and SKU limits so UX shows both. Internal heuristics: 1 session-credit == 2k soft tokens. If session uses <=2k tokens, consume 1 credit. If >2k, consume 1 credit + ceil((tokens-2k)/1k) token units. This keeps things simple and reduces friction.

Unit economics sensitivity table (quick):
- Assume session price = $0.01, infra cost per session = $0.0014 (from above): margin ~86%
- If model shifts to larger context (cost x2): infra session cost = $0.0028 -> margin ~72%
- If average session length increases 2x (1.4k tokens): infra doubles -> margin halves roughly.

Thoughts on tiers and anchoring psychology:
- Anchoring: show sessions as "conversations" with clear example scenarios (e.g., "300 conversations = ~5 per day")
- Offer a small free trial of 10 session credits so new users experience product without token confusion.
- Present token bundles as "extension packs" not default; keep STARTER page focused on sessions.

Edge cases / fraud / gaming:
- Long-running sessions that keep VRAM / KV cache hot => higher cost if we keep server-side state. Consider TTL: offline idle session cleanup after N minutes (configurable). Billers must have guardrails: max tokens per session without special approval.
- Heavy upload usage (files -> long contexts): route to per-token pricing or dedicated plan.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should session-credit soft budget be configurable per customer? (e.g., enterprise wants 10k soft tokens) Pros: flexibility. Cons: complexity for UI and SKU math.
- How to present refunds/unused credits on billing cycle end? Auto-rollover? Rollover encourages lower short-term revenue but improves stickiness.
- What are SLAs for burst capacity vs dedicated? Map to pricing tiers.
- Confirm infra cost ranges per model on Dedicated vs Hosted (get updated numbers from infra finance).

Concrete next steps (for me):
- Ask infra-finance for per-model 1k token cost table (optimize by quantization/sequence length) — add to spreadsheet. (linked: CONFLUENCE-PLANS-1423)
- Prototype UX mock for checkout copy: "Conversations vs Tokens" with example conversions (Ben to review).
- Run quick cohort sim: 2k users with distribution of session counts (Poisson?), compute revenue and cloud cost -> rough margin over 12 months.
- Draft one-pager for price experiment (A/B: sessions-only vs sessions + visible token top-ups). Tag GH-PR-9812.

Quick simulation idea (scratch):
- Assumed cohort: 2,000 paying users; 10% power users (avg 25 sessions/mo), 70% core (6 sessions/mo), 20% occasional (1 session/mo)
- Weighted avg sessions/user/mo = 0.1*25 + 0.7*6 + 0.2*1 = 2.5 + 4.2 + 0.2 = 6.9 sessions/mo
- Total sessions/mo = 13,800 -> infra cost = 13,800 * $0.0014 = $19.32/mo (~negligible) -> if we price at $0.01/session => revenue = $138/mo -> margin huge. But this is likely undercounting tail tokens. Need better tail model.

Notes-to-self: be conservative on cost multipliers (x3) when sizing experiments. Use 95th percentile token sizes for capacity planning, not mean.

Random heuristics / small ideas:
- Offer "session saver": opt-in compression/shorten prompts for 20% lower token consumption (opt-in, model may shorten phrasing). Could be a toggle that reduces cost for customer (and reduces our infra cost).
- For enterprise: sell "seat + session pool" — seat guarantees team access, pool consumed by the org. Simpler to bill and maps to internal purchasing patterns.

Final: this is intentionally rough. Want to convert to a one-pager and a short experiment spec. Keep this doc as the personal scratchpad; will move to shared drive planning once we stabilize numbers.

-- Samira
